entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Henry III, Count of Schauenburg-Holstein was a prominent figure in the medieval European landscape, playing a crucial role in the politics and religious dynamics of the 14th century. As Bishop of Osnabrück from 1402 to 1410, he navigated the complex web of ecclesiastical power struggles during the Great Schism. In 1404, he ascended to the position of Count of Holstein-Rendsburg, a title that reflected his family's influence in the region. His legacy extends beyond his own tenure, as he contributed to the shaping of the Hanseatic League's power dynamics and played a role in the ongoing struggle for control of the Holy Roman Empire.


 Henry III, Count of Schauenburg-Holstein's influence extended beyond his regional sphere, as he interacted with other notable figures of the time. His relationships with other prominent leaders, such as the Duke of Saxe-Lauenburg and the Archbishop of Bremen, had significant implications for the regional balance of power. Moreover, his efforts to strengthen the ties between the Holy Roman Empire and the Hanseatic League had lasting effects on the development of trade and commerce in the region.


 The legacy of Henry III, Count of Schauenburg-Holstein can be seen in the continued influence of the Schauenburg family on the politics of Holstein-Rendsburg. His successors continued to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the region, while his own actions laid the groundwork for the eventual rise of the Duchy of Schleswig.
